nodes.summary: For integers $a$, $d$, $t$ and $w$, if $|a| \le w$, $|a + d| \le w$ and $0 \le t \le d$, then $|a + t| \le w$.
nodes.title: Bound at an intermediate point, sum form

nodes.summary: For integers $a$, $d$, $t$ and $w$, if $|a| \le w$, $|a - d| \le w$ and $0 \le t \le d$, then $|a - t| \le w$.
nodes.title: Bound at an intermediate point, difference form

nodes.summary: With nonpositive substitution scores and gap score at most `-1`, an alignment scores at most minus its number of gap columns.
nodes.title: Alignment score is at most minus the number of gap columns

nodes.summary: Let $w, i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x$, $y$ be lists of lengths $m$ and $n$. If $|i - j| \le w$ and $|(i + m) - (j + n)| \le w$, then the band check of the diagonal alignment of $x$ and $y$ with width $w$ from offset $(i, j)$ is true.
nodes.title: The diagonal alignment stays in the band

nodes.summary: Let $w, i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A$ be an alignment. If the band check of $A$ with width $w$ from offset $(i, j)$ is true, then $|(i + p) - (j + q)| \le w$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of columns of $A$ whose first, respectively second, entry is present.
nodes.title: A passing band check bounds the final offset

nodes.summary: Let $w, i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a list of length $n$, and let $A$ be the alignment with one column for each element $a$ of $x$, in order, with first entry $a$ and empty second entry. If $|i - j| \le w$ and $|(i + n) - j| \le w$, then the band check of $A$ with width $w$ from offset $(i, j)$ is true.
nodes.title: Columns using only the first sequence stay in the band

nodes.summary: Let $w, i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $y$ be a list of length $n$, and let $A$ be the alignment with one column for each element $b$ of $y$, in order, with empty first entry and second entry $b$. If $|i - j| \le w$ and $|i - (j + n)| \le w$, then the band check of $A$ with width $w$ from offset $(i, j)$ is true.
nodes.title: Columns using only the second sequence stay in the band

nodes.summary: Along every prefix, the offset difference is at most the starting difference plus the number of gap columns: an alignment starting at `(i, j)` stays in the band of width `w` as soon as `|i - j| + gapColumns A ≤ w`.
nodes.title: An alignment with few gap columns stays in the band from its start

nodes.summary: Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$ be a band width. For natural numbers $i$, $j$ and an alignment $A$, the band check of $A$ with width $w$ from offset $(i, j)$ is true exactly when every prefix $P$ of $A$ (including the empty prefix and $A$ itself) satisfies $|(i + p) - (j + q)| \le w$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of columns of $P$ whose first, respectively second, entry is present.
nodes.title: Band check from a starting offset

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an integer substitution score on an alphabet, $g$ an integer gap score and $w \in \mathbb{N}$ a band width. For sequences $x$ and $y$ over the alphabet, if some alignment of $x$ and $y$ is banded with width $w$ and has score (under $\sigma$ and $g$) equal to the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ and $y$, then the banded score of $x$ and $y$ (under $\sigma$, $g$ and width $w$) is defined and equals their…
nodes.title: Banded alignment is exact when some optimal alignment is banded

nodes.summary: The banded optimum is exact when the optimal score is at least `-w` (optimal cost at most `w`), for nonpositive substitution scores and gap score at most `-1`: some optimal alignment exists and, by the band lemma, it is `w`-banded.
nodes.title: The banded optimum is exact

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an integer substitution score on an alphabet, $g$ an integer gap score and $w \in \mathbb{N}$ a band width. For sequences $x$ and $y$ over the alphabet and an integer $s$, if the banded score of $x$ and $y$ (under $\sigma$, $g$ and width $w$) is defined and equals $s$, then $s$ is at most the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: The banded score is at most the Needleman–Wunsch score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an integer substitution score on an alphabet, $g$ an integer gap score and $w \in \mathbb{N}$ a band width. For sequences $x$ and $y$ over the alphabet, of lengths $m$ and $n$, with $w < |m - n|$, the banded score of $x$ and $y$ (under $\sigma$, $g$ and width $w$) is undefined: no alignment of $x$ and $y$ is banded with width $w$.
nodes.title: No banded score when the lengths differ by more than the band width

nodes.summary: Fix a substitution score $\sigma$, assigning an integer $\sigma(a, b)$ to each pair of letters $a$, $b$, an integer gap score $g$ and a band width $w \in \mathbb{N}$. If two sequences $x$ and $y$ have lengths differing by at most $w$, that is $\bigl| |x| - |y| \bigr| \le w$, then the banded alignment score of $x$ and $y$ (for $\sigma$, $g$ and $w$) is defined: it equals some integer $s$.
nodes.title: The banded score is defined when the lengths are close

nodes.summary: Fix a substitution score $\sigma$, assigning an integer $\sigma(a, b)$ to each pair of letters $a$, $b$, an integer gap score $g$ and a band width $w \in \mathbb{N}$. The banded alignment score of two sequences $x$ and $y$ is the maximum, over all valid alignments of $x$ and $y$ that are banded with width $w$, of the (integer) alignment score with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$. It has no value (it is the empty…
nodes.title: Banded alignment score

nodes.summary: For sequences $x = x_1 \dots x_m$ and $y = y_1 \dots y_n$, let $k = \min(m, n)$. The diagonal alignment of $x$ and $y$ consists of the columns $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_k, y_k)$, which pair letters by position whether or not they are equal, followed by one column for each remaining letter of the longer sequence, in order, pairing that letter with a gap.
nodes.title: Diagonal alignment

nodes.summary: The number of gap columns of an alignment: columns with exactly one letter.
nodes.title: Number of gap columns of an alignment

nodes.summary: For all sequences $x$ and $y$, the diagonal alignment of $x$ and $y$ is a valid alignment of $x$ and $y$: none of its columns consists of two gaps, and deleting the gaps from its first and second rows gives $x$ and $y$ respectively.
nodes.title: The diagonal alignment is a valid alignment

nodes.summary: Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$. If two sequences $x$ and $y$ have lengths differing by at most $w$, that is $\bigl| |x| - |y| \bigr| \le w$, then the diagonal alignment of $x$ and $y$ is banded with width $w$.
nodes.title: The diagonal alignment is banded

nodes.summary: Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$. If $A$ is a valid alignment of sequences $x$ and $y$ and $A$ is banded with width $w$, then the lengths of $x$ and $y$ differ by at most $w$, that is $\bigl| |x| - |y| \bigr| \le w$.
nodes.title: Banded alignments force close lengths

nodes.summary: An alignment with at most `w` gap columns is `w`-banded.
nodes.title: An alignment with at most w gap columns is w-banded

nodes.summary: The band lemma (Ukkonen 1985): with nonpositive substitution scores and gap score at most `-1`, every alignment scoring at least `-w` (cost at most `w`) is `w`-banded.
nodes.title: The band lemma

nodes.summary: Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$. An alignment $A$ is banded with width $w$ when, for every prefix of $A$ (including the empty prefix and $A$ itself), the number of columns of that prefix with a letter in the first row and the number with a letter in the second row differ by at most $w$.
nodes.title: Banded alignments
Mathematical Biology

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
